# Standards inventory summary

<!-- Generated by npm run requirements:docs; edit standards/assessments.json for assessments. -->

This index covers SysML 2.0 Part 1 and KerML 1.0. It is a source inventory with
bounded evidence mappings. It is not a completed atomic-requirements review or a
conformance claim. Read [the method and remaining work](requirements.md), or use
[the searchable inventory](requirements.html).

## Evidence mapped so far

76 bounded assessments map 132 executable cases and 0 planned cases.
Linked tests are evidence for the assessment wording only. They do not qualify
a whole source clause, its descendants, or a named constraint merely because it
belongs to the same metaclass. Product robustness cases are identified separately.

| CONNECTION-ENDPOINTS | standard | partial / partial | 2 / 3 / 0 / 0 | KERNEL-015 isolates uncertainty to each end ownership subtree. A broken peer or unrelated connection-body member no longer masks a fully resolved end. Missing first/middle/last links, ambiguous names, n-ary ends, KerML connectors and split flow prefix/redefinition ownership have regression cases. Unresolved multiplicity references inside an end still conservatively block that end; implicit ends remain unsupported. Source references and diagnostics remain separate evidence, and endpoint display spelling can still represent a retained prefix rather than full original source. An ownership index visits each marked node once, with shared-ancestor and cycle-termination checks. Native/WASM tests retain the full previous mixed corpus and unresolved-import variant; CONN-004 fills the last available document slot in the 32-document guard workspace, and CONN-005 is additionally tested in a two-dialect parity request. This is bounded target projection, not qualification of whole-model validity, all contextual name resolution, flow compatibility, end typing, connector constraints, complete graphical notation or every syntax-recovery shape. Mixed-workspace qualification also requires sharing immutable checked callee projections to avoid repeated copies within the unchanged work allowance; this preserves existing arithmetic and predicate evidence without expanding their semantic scope. |
| SOURCE-NAMES | standard | partial / partial | 1 / 0 / 0 / 0 | Only name spelling relates to the standard here; byte/UTF-16 coordinate fidelity is a product guarantee. |
| SOURCE-RECOVERY | product | partial / partial | 0 / 1 / 0 / 0 | Error recovery policy is a product requirement; the linked clause supplies context, not a recovery conformance rule. |
| ROBUSTNESS-CYCLES | product | partial / partial | 0 / 0 / 2 / 0 | Termination and retained declarations do not establish a semantic verdict on cyclic models. |
| MEMBERSHIP-ENUMERATION | product | partial / partial | 4 / 3 / 1 / 0 | Schema 3 exposes explicit owned/inherited bindings and checked imported closure with contextual visibility, ordered identities and explicit unknown results. Missing endpoints, incomplete Type providers, inline filters and syntax recovery do not certify empty closure. General metadata/filter predicates, all contextual resolution, implicit construction and complete metamodel traversal remain open. Complete results certify this bounded query, not whole-model validity. |
| MULTIPLICITY-EXPRESSION | product | partial / partial | 17 / 12 / 2 / 0 | Static package providers support checked arithmetic and conditionals with Boolean literals, references and nested tests. MULT-016 now passes; selected branches preserve exact bounds and unselected unbound/undefined values are not executed. Unavailable or non-Boolean conditions, invalid selected values, recursive/ineligible branches and shadowed designated operators remain unknown. General value equality, other control operators, direct function execution and all contextual/evaluation semantics remain unqualified. MULT-020/021 retain independent exact arithmetic and conditional bounds alongside unresolved classifier bases; direct and transitive dependents remain incomplete. Malformed relationship evidence, dependent dynamic families and other unqualified configurations can still prevent shared publication. This is bounded proof isolation, not complete execution or general incremental analysis. MULT-022/023 qualify combined arithmetic/conditional range endpoints, aliases, repeated providers and invalid endpoints using checked evidence shared within one query. KERNEL-006 qualifies first direct range, alias and repeated-endpoint queries over the full pinned library after implied relationships are published, without preceding proof queries. Callee signatures share checked evidence; every supplied binding is rechecked. Other cold entry paths and more complex expressions can still exhaust the unchanged allowance; reuse does not qualify every composition or a global cache. KERNEL-007 adds finite exact numeric <, <=, > and >= predicates, with designated function identity and checked positional evidence. MULT-024/025 cover each relation, large integers, exact rationals, aliases, nested/lazy selection and refused operands/endpoints. Approximate real, infinity, quantity, ordered string, sequence and general function comparisons remain unqualified. Arithmetic intermediates can exceed i128 through exact rationals; exported bounds retain the signed-128-bit limit. KERNEL-008 adds equality/sameness (==, !=, ===, !==) for Boolean pairs or finite exact numeric pairs, eager Boolean not/xor/&/\| and conditional and/or/implies. All deferred operands retain complete model-level eligibility and reciprocal wrapper evidence; only required values are executed. MULT-026/027/028 cover exact scalar values, all Boolean truth tables, eager versus skipped unavailable values, nested expressions and negative operand/endpoint guards. Cross-domain Boolean/numeric equality, nonempty sequence/occurrence values, quantities, approximate numbers and general function dispatch remain unqualified. This is a bounded provider execution certificate, not whole-model type validity. KERNEL-009 adds explicit empty NullExpression values and lazy ?? over the admitted exact scalar domain. MULT-029/030 distinguish null and () from zero, Boolean false, unavailable providers and execution failure, and cover nested composition, aliases, skipped/selected operands and numeric endpoint restrictions. Every operand still requires eligibility and reciprocal deferred-wrapper proof. Approximate arithmetic results, including exponent overflow to infinity and underflow to zero, are refused. Null is an intermediate value, not a numeric endpoint or absence certificate. The combined old/new workspace and unresolved-import variant retain their earlier assertions. Same-transaction static-prefix reuse skips an unused library-name rebuild while preserving physical-authority and recipe checks and the unchanged work allowance. Larger compositions may still exhaust that allowance. KERNEL-010 adds ==, !=, === and !== for explicit empty pairs and empty versus admitted Boolean or exact numeric scalars, with both operands successfully executed before comparison. MULT-031/032 qualify both operand orders, aliases and coalescing/conditional/logical composition, preserving unknown for unavailable operands, failures, unsupported domains and invalid endpoints. Two earlier null-equality expectations now correctly evaluate to 7. Empty comparison does not certify occurrence identity, general sequence equality or whole-model type validity. Dynamic staging prepares all rows before atomic ownership registration and reuses the private result-family ownership view; it no longer clones the complete prefix twice. Late invalid owners, identity changes and exhausted budgets leave the prior view intact. The full integration corpus remains combined and the work allowance is unchanged. KERNEL-011 adds decoded LiteralString values, string-pair equality and sameness, binary string concatenation and empty-versus-string comparisons. MULT-033/034 qualify Unicode and standard escapes, exact character preservation, aliases and conditional/coalescing/logical composition. An empty string remains present; string values never coerce to numeric endpoints. String copies, concatenation allocation and comparison charge UTF-8 bytes to the unchanged cumulative work allowance. String ordering, mixed-domain operations, general StringFunctions calls, complete lexical conformance and whole-model type validity remain unqualified. The combined publication path consumes its freshly audited static prefix without a redundant second audit, and warm-prefix collision checks use the complete raw identity index. Remapped identities, malformed rows, independent entry paths and work-limit refusals retain explicit regression coverage. |

| LEXICAL-NAMES | standard | partial / partial | 4 / 3 / 0 / 0 | KERNEL-012 qualifies form-feed token separation and the seven KerML Table 4 escape forms for names and strings in both dialects. Nonstandard escapes, including \r, and all 65 raw C0/C1 controls produce syntax errors with complete Unicode character ranges. LF is the decoded newline representation on every host. Lexer tests retain complete token coverage, EOF/trailing-escape termination and comment boundaries. Public tests check byte/UTF-16 coordinates, following-declaration recovery and conservative workspace cardinality invalidation. Full Unicode printability, arbitrary line-terminator encodings, every numeric terminal and complete lexical/grammar conformance remain unqualified. The formatter and textual editing APIs are outside the current facade contract. |
| CARDINALITY-RECOVERY | product | partial / partial | 0 / 5 / 0 / 0 | Conservative workspace-wide invalidation also affects otherwise valid types until syntax errors are fixed; precise dependency-based invalidation remains future work. |
| NUMERIC-LITERALS | standard | partial / partial | 0 / 2 / 2 / 0 | KERNEL-013 covers decimal/exponential terminal boundaries and real-value token composition, leading-dot forms, signed exponents, unary signs, range delimiters, whitespace/notes, malformed forms and recovery in both dialects. Original source, spans and public valueExpression text remain unchanged; internal real values exclude trivia and lowering retains exact digits through JSON number or string representation. A product robustness check rejects scales outside the unchanged +/-100000 conversion allowance, including i64::MIN, without wrapping or panicking. Those resource limits are not language syntax limits. Fractional multiplicities retain their semantic diagnostic. The facade still refuses real-valued and extreme-exponent bounds. This does not qualify all numeric contexts, arbitrary expressions, general real-valued execution, a public value/AST API, normative interchange, full Unicode or complete lexical conformance. |
| RESERVED-WORDS | standard | partial / partial | 2 / 2 / 0 / 0 | KERNEL-014 checks all 128 SysML and 101 KerML reserved-word entries through five syntax contexts: long names, short names, alias names, alias targets and qualified expression references. Tests cover quoting, upper-case and identifier suffix/prefix boundaries, the other dialect's vocabulary, Unicode diagnostic coordinates, constructor AST distinction, public query/JSON round-trip and syntax recovery. The existing reservation of new is retained as an explicit compatibility policy: it is missing from both published lists but used by the constructor production; OMG SYSML21-641 and KERML11-200 remain open at the 2026-10-17 review. That ambiguity is not claimed as normative qualification. The four public cases exercise representative reference-resolution and recovery contexts, not every keyword in every semantic context. Full grammar, contextual name resolution, Unicode printability, formatter/editing and constructor execution remain unqualified. No production parser behavior or engine version changes in this increment. |

This is bounded target-kind validation, not qualification of the complete validateTransitionUsageSuccession obligation: missing-succession cases, every target of nonbinary/raw connector forms, implied ends and all malformed ownership configurations remain open. Resolution diagnostics remain independently visible. |

## Sources and extraction checks

All numbered clauses reconcile between PDF bookmarks, the printed TOC and body
headings. The importer checks pinned source bytes and reports counts for every
indexed XMI type. Five printed grammar headers omit an equals sign; these have
explicit extraction exceptions and are included. Prose candidates locate modal
passages by digest; they are not automatically classified as normative obligations.
